docs.title: cfdna-tissue-enrichment
docs.text:
Which tissues and cell types does a group difference in plasma cfDNA coverage come from? This tool answers that with one standardised method against interchangeable chromatin-accessibility atlases: ENCODE tissues, TCGA tumours, the maternal–fetal interface, and any atlas you add.

cfDNA fragment files ──► clean hg38 bins ──► GC-corrected, detrended coverage
                                                   │
          atlas layers (C, T, W, …) ──► track specificity per bin
                                                   │
                              ┌────────────────────┴────────────────────┐
                            sample                                differential
                  per sample, all bins vs a              per bin group effect, then
                  reference group                         tissue enrichment of it
  • Same method for every project. Only the panel changes: which atlas layers and which pre-registered tracks.
  • Two readouts. A per-sample score (sample) and a group-level enrichment (differential). Both use every bin, with no bin selection, and agree closely (track rankings r ≈ 0.91–0.97 across the benchmarks).
  • Group designs from a single comparison to factorial (e.g. term/preterm × SGA/non-SGA) with covariates.
  • Clean by construction. ENCODE blacklist, gaps, high-N and low-mappability bins are removed before anything is counted.
Panel Layers Use prenatal ENCODE tissues (C) + maternal–fetal interface snATAC (W) pregnancy outcomes, placental signal tumor ENCODE tissues (C) + TCGA tumour ATAC (T) any cancer; set --primary for your tumour type glioma C + T, glioma / CNS tracks pre-registered GBM / LGG projects pan C + T + W exploration, nothing pre-registered

Start with Install and quick start. The method is described in Method.

Developed in the EpiFluid Lab (Northwestern University), from cfdna-chromatin-xai.

docs.title: Add a new atlas
docs.text:
A new atlas is a new layer. The method does not change.

  1. Make the layer table on the existing grid: reference/hg38/layer_<ID>_50kb.csv.gz (and _10kb), with a key column matching grid_<bin>.csv.gz (e.g. chr1:900000-950000) and one numeric column per track. Any openness scale works (peak coverage, signal, CPM); specificity re-standardises each bin across the layer's tracks. Rules:
    • one source and one assay per layer (do not mix DNase and ATAC in one layer);
    • build from hg38 data, or place windows on hg38 natively rather than lifting bin by bin where possible;
    • bins with no data stay NaN, never 0.
  2. Describe it in reference/hg38/layers.json (name, assay, n_tracks, source, values, provenance, citation; track_meta for an optional per-track metadata CSV).
  3. Use it from a panel ("layers": ["C", "<ID>"]) and add groups, axes and primary tracks as needed.
  4. Check it with a known contrast before using it on outcomes, and record the result in the docs.

build/build_layers.py shows how the C, T and W layers were made and is the template for new ones.

Planned layers: Calderon 2019 immune cell ATAC (resting and stimulated), Corces 2016 haematopoiesis ATAC (monocyte, erythroid, progenitors), peripheral-neutrophil ATAC (GSE153520), CATlas adult snATAC (endothelium, hepatocyte), GSE174367 brain snATAC.

docs.title: Benchmarks (v0.2.0, 2026-11-05)
docs.text: Benchmarks with known or expected answers, run with the tumor or glioma panel (layers C + T), modes sample and differential (sets was removed in 0.2.0; see method). Each run folder also has ranked_<effect>.png bar plots of every track. Scripts are in benchmarks/; result tables in benchmarks/results/.

docs.title: 1. PRAD in-silico mixtures (hg19): does the method find tumour DNA, and how little?
docs.text:
Design. Fragments from a prostate cancer plasma sample (PRAD_14230, ichorCNA tumour fraction 46.5%) mixed into a healthy person's plasma (HD45) at 0, 0.5, 1, 2, 5, 10 and 20% tumour fraction; 10 M and 30 M fragments; 3 replicates each. A second healthy person (HD46) at 0% shows person-to-person variation. Detection = all 3 replicates beyond every unspiked sample (HD45 and HD46) at that depth. All files hg19 (native build of C and T).

Depth Mode Spearman, T_PRAD vs tumour fraction Rank of T_PRAD by |rho| among all 101 tracks Detection limit 10 M sample −0.88 1 2% 30 M sample −0.94 1 2%
  • T_PRAD is the most tumour-fraction-responsive of all 101 tracks (TCGA, ENCODE tissues and cell types, groups) at both depths.
  • Direction: more tumour DNA lowers coverage at the tumour's specific open regions (negative score). Read tumour tracks this way: lower = more tumour-derived signal.
  • The removed sets mode (top-1,000 bins) had detection limits of 20% (10 M) and 5% (30 M).
  • Caveat: the null has only two healthy people. The earlier benchmark with four people showed that person-to-person variation, not depth, sets the floor, so real-world limits will be higher than 2%.

Differential mode on the mixtures (spiked ≥ 5% vs unspiked, 9 vs 6 samples per depth):

Depth All-bins rho for T_PRAD (rank among all 101 tracks) p Top-2,000 "down" bins: T_PRAD specificity rank among 23 TCGA tracks p 10 M −0.044 (most negative, 1st) 0.005 1st of 23 0.015 30 M −0.076 (1st) < 0.005 1st of 23 < 0.005

Differential mode recovers the tumour type too: bins that lose coverage with tumour DNA are the most PRAD-specific.

docs.title: 2. Cabat pan-cancer cohort (hg38): does each cancer light up its own track?
docs.text:
Design. 139 cases (pancreatic 28, lung 23, breast 22, prostate 21, colorectal 18, ovary 12, liver 8, stomach 7) and 139 matched controls, QC-pass. Each cancer type vs all controls, adjusted for batch and sex; own TCGA track as primary (pancreas / ovary have no TCGA track, so the ENCODE tissue was used). ichorCNA tumour fractions are mostly below ~3%.

Cancer Own track sample t (p) differential rho (p) Spearman of sample score with ichorCNA TF (cases) Breast T_BRCA 3.18 (0.002), rank 1/23 0.023 (<0.001), rank 1/23 −0.30 (p 0.18) Stomach T_STAD 2.61 (0.012), rank 3/23 0.017 (0.03) −0.18 (p 0.70, n 7) Liver T_LIHC −2.49 (0.017) −0.043 (0.01) 0.55 (p 0.16, n 8) Prostate T_PRAD 1.07 (0.28) 0.013 (0.23) −0.06 (p 0.80) Colorectal T_COAD 0.21 (0.83) 0.001 (0.84) −0.17 (p 0.50) Lung T_LUSC / T_LUAD −1.23 / −1.13 n.s. 0.13 / 0.18 Pancreatic C_pancreas −0.83 n.s. 0.01 Ovary C_ovary −3.93 (<0.001) −0.086 (<0.001) −0.22 (p 0.48)
  • No diagonal. Most cancer types share the same pattern of TCGA tracks (see the matrix rows), so the main case-vs-control difference in this cohort is common to all cancers, not tumour-type specific. At ichorCNA fractions of ~1–3%, tumour-specific DNA is near the detection limit found in benchmark 1.
  • Direction matters. Benchmark 1 shows tumour DNA lowers the own-track score. Own-track changes in that direction: liver (T_LIHC, sample t −2.49, p 0.017; differential p 0.01) and ovary (C_ovary, negative in all three modes, p < 0.001). Breast (T_BRCA) and stomach (T_STAD) are significant in the opposite direction, so they are not tumour-derived signal; they follow the shared case/control shift.
  • No dose-response with ichorCNA tumour fraction within cases. The own-track sample score is negative (the tumour direction) in 5 of 8 cancer types, but none is significant. (The removed sets mode had shown significant correlations for stomach and lung; they do not hold in the all-bins score.) At ichorCNA fractions of ~1–3% the tumour signal is below what this cohort can resolve.
  • The shared pattern needs follow-up before biological interpretation: cases and controls may differ in collection era or processing, which no covariate here captures.

docs.title: Immune and blood tracks (ENCODE layer) in Cabat
docs.text:
Track Cases vs controls Strongest (permutation p < 0.05) B, NK, CD4 T, CD8 T, myeloid progenitor, spleen, thymus lower in 94–100% of cancer type × mode tests prostate (all, sample; B, NK, progenitor, spleen, thymus also differential), pancreatic (B, NK, progenitor, spleen, thymus), colorectal and lung (progenitor, spleen, thymus) Neutrophil lower (88%) prostate (both modes), pancreatic and colorectal (sample) Monocyte slightly higher stomach (sample t = 2.24)

With the mixture-benchmark direction (more DNA from a cell type lowers coverage at its specific bins), cancer plasma in this cohort carries relatively more blood-cell-derived cfDNA, especially lymphoid and progenitor, than controls. This matches the shared, non-tumour-specific case/control shift seen on the TCGA tracks. Collection or processing differences between cases and controls could produce the same pattern. Table: benchmarks/results/cabat_immune_tracks.csv.

docs.title: 3. GBM cohorts (hg38, one library batch each)
docs.text:
Comparison Panel n Result GBM (IDH-wt) vs schwannoma glioma 20 vs 16 No glioma or CNS track significant in any mode (T_GBM sample t −0.03, p 0.97). Neutrophil lower in GBM (differential rho −0.087, p 0.04; q 0.36). Metastatic breast vs schwannoma tumor 10 vs 16 T_BRCA lower in the expected (tumour) direction in all modes, strongest in sample mode (t −1.80, p 0.08, rank 4/23); not significant at this n. Monocyte-specific bins over-represented among bins losing coverage (top-bin p 0.035). Progression vs pseudo-progression glioma 5 vs 5 Nothing significant (all q ≥ 0.84).

GBM releases little tumour DNA into plasma, so the absence of a glioma signal is expected at these sizes; the method does not invent one. The metastatic breast comparison points the right way but needs more samples.

docs.title: 4. Null calibration (Cabat controls, random labels)
docs.text:
Mode Runs Mean share of tracks at p < 0.05 Max in one run sample 10 5.0% 16.8% differential 3 0.3% 1.0%

On average the per-sample modes are calibrated (~5%). Single runs can show many tracks at once because tracks are correlated (one chance shift moves related tissues together); use the q-values and the primary-track correction. Differential mode is conservative.

docs.title: Take-aways
docs.text:
1. The method recovers tumour-type-specific signal when tumour DNA is ≥ 2%, in both modes (sample per sample; differential at the group level), and the tumour track is the top responder among all 101 tracks.
  2. Tumour tracks go down with more tumour DNA; a significant change in the other direction is not tumour signal.
  3. In low-fraction real cohorts, expect shared, non-specific case/control shifts; pre-register tracks and check dose-response with an independent tumour-fraction estimate (ichorCNA) before interpreting.

• sets mode removed. Two modes remain, sample (per sample) and differential (group level); both use every bin and agree closely. Why: method, section 5. --set-size removed; a run without groups now stops with a message instead of falling back to sets.
  • Benchmark scripts and write-up updated to the two modes.

• Ranked bar plots of every track for each effect in all three modes (two panels like the cfdna-chromatin-xai plot, coloured by track type), --bar-top, and a plot command to redraw them for a finished run.
  • Benchmark runs re-plotted with the new figures.

• hg19 reference (layers C and T; clean grid from the hg19 ENCODE blacklist v2, UCSC gaps, N > 10%, CRG 50-mer mappability < 0.80).
  • count command and --cache: per-sample counts computed once (parallel) and reused.
  • MAPQ column detected from a fragment-file header (FinaleDB files: column 5).
  • Benchmarks: PRAD mixtures (hg19), Cabat pan-cancer (hg38), null calibration.

• First standalone release, generalised from pregnancy_tissue_kit v1.1.
  • Layers C (ENCODE DNase), T (TCGA ATAC), W (maternal–fetal interface snATAC) on hg38, 50 kb and 10 kb.
  • Panels prenatal, tumor, glioma, pan.
  • Modes sets, sample, differential; factorial designs with covariates and stratified permutations.
  • Random bin sets matched on GC × mappability; top-bin p-values from label permutations.

docs.title: Method
docs.text: Every panel runs exactly these steps; only the atlas layers and the pre-registered tracks differ.

docs.title: 1. Coverage
docs.text:
1. Grid. hg38 autosomes in 50 kb (45,595 bins) or 10 kb (241,026 bins). Bins are removed if they overlap the ENCODE blacklist (ENCFF356LFX) by any amount, overlap an assembly gap, are > 10% N, or have 45-mer mappability < 0.80.
  2. Counting. Fragment midpoints per bin; MAPQ ≥ 30 and length 50–500 bp. Midpoints in removed bins are dropped.
  3. Normalisation (identical to cfdna-enrich prep.py): log2(CPM + 1) → LOWESS on bin GC (frac 0.10, 3 iterations, level kept) → subtraction of a centred ~2 Mb rolling median per chromosome (removes copy number and other broad trends).

docs.title: 2. Track specificity
docs.text:
For each layer separately (one source, one assay), every bin's openness is standardised across that layer's tracks, and each track's specificity is its value minus the mean of the layer's other tracks. Specificity says how much more open a bin is in that track than in the other tracks of the same layer. Layers are never mixed in this step, so DNase and ATAC values are not compared directly.

Panels can add derived tracks:

  • groups: mean specificity of member tracks (e.g. Wgroup_trophoblast_SCT_VCT, Tgroup_glioma);
  • axes: mean of one set of tracks minus another (e.g. origin_fetal_specific); a cross-layer axis (e.g. glioma_vs_blood, TCGA tracks minus ENCODE blood tracks) is allowed but marked exploratory.

Within-layer means relative to the layer

T_GBM specificity is "open in GBM more than in the other TCGA cancer types", not "more than in blood". Use a cross-layer axis or the C_ blood tracks alongside it when the question is tumour vs blood.

docs.title: 3. The two modes
docs.text:
mode per-sample score method sample yes Each bin is turned into a z-score against the reference group (median, 1.4826 × MAD; reference samples left out of their own reference when ≥ 4). E = Spearman correlation of a sample's z over all bins with the track's specificity. Uses all bins, nothing selected. differential no Each bin is fitted with the group model (moderated t). Per track: (a) all bins: Spearman correlation of bin t with specificity; (b) top bins: mean specificity of the 2,000 bins most up and most down. Both are tested against label permutations (bins refitted and top bins re-selected each time). A z against GC × mappability matched random bins is reported for description only.

Positive values mean the same in both modes: more coverage, in cases (or in that sample), at bins specific to the track.

docs.title: 4. Group design and tests
docs.text:
• --factor COLUMN:REFERENCE:CASE defines a two-level factor; repeat for factorial designs. The reference group is every factor at its reference level.
  • Effect tests (sample mode): OLS of each score on the factors + covariates; p from OLS and from permutations of one factor's labels within levels of the other factors (covariates stay with their samples).
  • Pairwise tests: every other group vs the reference group (difference, AUC, Mann–Whitney p, permutation p).
  • Multiple testing: BH across all tracks (q_perm) and separately across the panel's primary tracks (q_perm_primary).

docs.title: 5. Why there is no sets mode
docs.text: Versions ≤ 0.1.2 had a third mode, sets: mean coverage over each track's top-1,000 specific bins minus random bins matched on GC and mappability (the original cfdna-chromatin-xai marker method). It was removed in 0.2.0. Across 11 benchmarks its track rankings agreed only moderately with the other modes (r 0.35–0.63, against 0.91–0.97 between sample and differential), tracks significant in two modes sometimes went in opposite directions with sets the odd one out, and it was the least sensitive mode in the PRAD mixtures (detection limit 20% at 10 M fragments, against 2% for sample). Top specific bins differ from matched random bins in more than GC and mappability (gene density, replication timing), so part of a sets score is not cell-type signal.

docs.title: 6. Why permutation p-values for top bins
docs.text: Top differential bins are selected from noisy data, so they are not exchangeable with random bins even when GC and mappability are matched. On null data, matched-random p-values flagged 6–14% of tracks at p < 0.05, against ~6% for the permutation p-values. The permutation null repeats the selection on shuffled labels.

docs.text: file content qc.csv, qc.png fragments read / used / in grid, median length, short fraction (100–150 bp), zero bins, low-depth flag design_matrix.csv the model: intercept, factor indicators, covariates sample/scores_E.csv samples × tracks: E vs the reference group sample/effect_tests.csv per track × effect: beta, t, p_ols, p_perm, q_perm, q_perm_primary sample/pairwise_vs_reference.csv each group vs the reference group: n, difference, AUC, p_mannwhitney, p_perm, q values */scores_heatmap.png, */primary_by_group.png per-sample heatmap; primary tracks by group */ranked_<effect>.png every track ranked, two panels (lower / higher coverage in cases), coloured by type (immune/blood, tissue, TCGA, derived); sample: group-effect t on E, differential: all-bins rho; * permutation p < 0.05, ** and q < 0.10. Redraw with cfdna-tissue-enrich plot --out RUN [--top N] differential/enrichment_all_bins.csv (+ .png) per effect × track: Spearman rho, p_perm, q_perm, q_perm_primary differential/enrichment_top_bins.csv per effect × direction × track: mean specificity of top bins, p_perm, q values; z_vs_matched_random with GC / mappability balance (descriptive) differential/bin_effects.csv.gz per effect × bin: moderated t and p run_manifest.json version, panel definition, layer provenance, design, every parameter

docs.title: Reading the results
docs.text:
• Scores are relative. They compare coverage at a track's specific bins with other bins in the same samples. Compare groups; do not read a value as a fraction of cfDNA.
  • Check the direction with a known contrast first. Whether more DNA from a cell type raises or lowers coverage at its specific bins depends on assay and depth. Examples: pregnant vs non-pregnant (placental tracks), high vs low tumour fraction (tumour tracks), early vs late gestation.
  • Agreement across modes is the strongest evidence. sample is per-sample; differential is group level. A track moving the same way in both is more convincing than one significant in a single mode.
  • Small groups. With < 8 per group, report effect sizes and AUC rather than p-values alone. Differential mode needs residual df ≥ 8; the log warns when lower.
  • Covariates. Adjust for what moves the tissue mix: gestational age in pregnancy; age, sex and batch in most cohorts.

docs.title: Limits
docs.text:
• hg38 only so far (a T2T build is planned).
  • The C and T layers come from an hg19 atlas moved to hg38 by bin midpoint (10 kb); W was placed on hg38 natively.
  • W windows are not peaks; at 50 kb their signal is diluted, which is why everything is based on specificity.
  • Seven W cell types have mixed fetal / maternal origin (dNK, T, B, FB, pvSMC, cDC, Ery); they are kept as tracks but excluded from the origin axis.
  • Differential mode's moderated t uses a fixed prior (4 df, median variance), a simple stand-in for limma.

docs.title: Layers
docs.text: hg38: C, T, W. hg19: C, T (the atlas's original build; W is not built for hg19). Choose with --build hg19.

docs.title: hg38
docs.text:
ID Layer Assay Tracks Source Notes C ENCODE tissues and cell types DNase-seq 73 ENCODE DNase narrowPeak (72 biosamples: tissues, blood cells, endothelium, trophoblast) + one neutrophil track; cfdna-chromatin-xai openness atlas 10 kb lifted from hg19 by bin midpoint; 50 kb hg38 provenance not documented T TCGA tumours ATAC-seq 23 TCGA-ATAC cancer-type peak calls (Corces et al., Science 2018) split from the same atlas file as C W Maternal–fetal interface snATAC-seq pseudobulk 32 Wang et al., Nature 653:167–179 (2026); 5 kb window counts prepared by Paz Polak placed on hg38 natively; erythroid dropped (67 nuclei)

Track names in outputs are <layer>_<track>, e.g. C_placenta, T_GBM, W_SCT. Cell-type metadata for W (origin, purity, nuclei) is in reference/hg38/tracks_W.csv. Full provenance is in reference/hg38/layers.json.

docs.title: Panels
docs.text: Panels live in panels/*.json. A panel lists layers, derived tracks and pre-registered primary tracks.

docs.title: prenatal (C + W)
docs.text:
• Groups: Wgroup_trophoblast_SCT_VCT, Wgroup_EVT, Wgroup_decidual_stroma, Wgroup_maternal_immune, Wgroup_maternal_endothelial, Wgroup_fetal_endothelial_stroma.
  • Axis: origin_fetal_specific (11 clean fetal minus 7 clean maternal cell types; purity ≥ 0.90, ≥ 500 nuclei) and its mirror origin_maternal_specific.
  • Primary: the four main W groups, the two origin tracks, C_placenta, C_trophoblast cell, C_neutrophil.

docs.title: tumor (C + T)
docs.text:
• Groups: Tgroup_glioma, Tgroup_kidney, Tgroup_lung, Tgroup_gastrointestinal, Tgroup_squamous.
  • No primary tracks: set --primary for the tumour type under study.

docs.title: glioma (C + T)
docs.text:
• As tumor, plus the exploratory cross-layer axis glioma_vs_blood (TCGA GBM/LGG minus ENCODE blood cells).
  • Primary: Tgroup_glioma, T_GBM, T_LGG, C_brain, C_frontal cortex, C_spinal cord, C_neutrophil, C_CD14-positive monocyte, glioma_vs_blood.

docs.title: pan (C + T + W)
docs.text: All groups from the other panels, no primary tracks. For exploration.

docs.title: Make your own panel
docs.text:
Copy a panel JSON and edit it. Fields:

{
 "name": "my_panel",
 "description": "one line",
 "layers": ["C", "T"],
 "groups": {"Tgroup_glioma": {"layer": "T", "members": ["GBM", "LGG"]}},
 "axes": {"glioma_vs_blood": {"plus_layer": "T", "plus": ["GBM", "LGG"],
                              "minus_layer": "C", "minus": ["neutrophil", "B cell"]}},
 "primary": ["Tgroup_glioma", "T_GBM", "C_neutrophil"]
}

Run with --panel path/to/my_panel.json. Fix the primary list before looking at outcome data.

docs.title: Install
docs.text:
git clone <repo-url> cfdna-tissue-enrichment && cd cfdna-tissue-enrichment
conda env create -f environment.yml && conda activate cfdna-tissue-enrichment
pip install -e .                      # provides the `cfdna-tissue-enrich` command

Python ≥ 3.9 with numpy, pandas, scipy, statsmodels and matplotlib. No internet or cluster paths are needed at run time. The hg38 reference (reference/hg38/, ~80 MB) ships with the repository.

docs.title: Smoke test
docs.text: bash tests/smoke_test.sh              # every panel on the example data + a reproducibility check

docs.title: Inputs
docs.text:
Sample sheet (CSV), one row per sample:

column required meaning sample_id yes unique name frag_path yes fragment file; absolute or relative to the sheet group columns for group analyses one column per two-level factor, e.g. birth = term / preterm, sga = nonSGA / SGA covariates no e.g. gestational_age_weeks, age, sex, batch

Fragment files: one fragment per line, tab-separated, plain or .gz, aligned to hg38: chrom start end [MAPQ] [...]. MAPQ is read from column 4 when numeric (--mapq-col N to change, 0 for none). FinaleDB fragment files work directly. Recommended depth: ≥ 5 M fragments at 50 kb, ≥ 20 M at 10 kb.

docs.title: Run
docs.text:
# pregnancy, 2 x 2 design, reference group = term non-SGA
cfdna-tissue-enrich run --panel prenatal --samples samples.csv --out results/ \
    --factor birth:term:preterm --factor sga:nonSGA:SGA --covariates gestational_age_weeks,bmi,batch:cat

# glioma vs controls
cfdna-tissue-enrich run --panel glioma --samples samples.csv --out results/ \
    --group diagnosis --reference-level control --case GBM --covariates age,sex

# another cancer: tumor panel with your own pre-registered tracks
cfdna-tissue-enrich run --panel tumor --samples samples.csv --out results/ \
    --group diagnosis --reference-level control --case PRAD --primary T_PRAD,C_neutrophil

cfdna-tissue-enrich panels                     # list panels
cfdna-tissue-enrich tracks --panel prenatal    # list a panel's tracks; * = primary

docs.title: Main options
docs.text: option default meaning --panel pan panel name or a panel JSON path --modes sample,differential either or both; both need groups (--factor or --group) --factor — COLUMN:REFERENCE:CASE, repeatable --group, --reference-level, --case — shortcut for one factor --interaction off factor × factor terms --covariates — comma-separated; numeric with ≥ 6 values = linear, else categorical; force with :num / :cat --primary panel's list pre-registered tracks (own BH correction) --bin 50kb 50kb or 10kb --top-n 2000 differential mode, bins per direction --n-perm, --n-perm-bins 2000, 200 permutations for score tests / differential mode --seed 17 same inputs + seed = identical output
